newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Plasson share offer encounters problems.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Plasson share offer encounters problems.

text.p: A 20 million pound sterling ($31 million) share offering by Israeli plastic-products maker Plasson has run into difficulties, apparently because of political concerns stemming from recent gunbattles between Israelis and Palestinians.

As of Friday, about 1.9 million pounds ($3 million) of the initial public offering was still unsold and the offering price had fallen to about 1.5 pounds, Shaul Ashkenazi, Plasson's managing director, told Reuters. The offering was expected to sell at 1.55 to 1.6 pounds.
He estimated that over 20 percent of equity had been sold to date, but that leaves Plasson short of the London Stock Exchange's minimum-float requirement of 25 percent.
The Israeli daily Maariv reported that concerns stemming from the violence which killed 73 people led to cancellations.
Ashkenazi would not directly blame the problem on political concerns in the market in the wake of the bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians.

But, he noted: "We had all the orders in hand Thursday (before the violence broke out)." He refused to comment on whether talks due to begin between Israeli and Palestinian officials on Sunday might improve sentiment.
Maariv said the London sponsors of the offering hope to complete the IPO during this week.
This would have been the first full listing of an Israeli company on the London Stock Exchange.
Last week another Israeli company, Nechustan Metals, postponed an offering on London's Alternative Investment Market scheduled for November to early next year due to the violence.
